description: Wires the Frobenius symmetrized constituent (h_Z/e_Z) into the canonical linear binding B=scale·(tr_free−tr_atom) for D/T/³He/⁴He. KEY STRUCTURAL RESULT: free and bound carry the SAME identical-particle symmetrization, so in the log-ratio form B_log=scale·log(tr_free/tr_atom) the free factor S_free=(h_Z h_N)/(τ^Z τ^N) CANCELS against the bound S_atom — symmetrizing tr_free ALONE is inconsistent (a spurious O(1) shift). The binding signal of identical-particle exchange is the residual log(S_free/S_atom), i.e. the exact block-swapped atom trace (task-1: |G|⁻¹Σ_{σ∈S_Z×S_N} tr_M(W_atom·σ)). Reports both candidate scales (Q_β, E_0); S_free per isotope (⁴He bosonic 2.47×) shows the exchange magnitude. tr_atom for D/T/³He/⁴He from binding-canonical.witness.json.

structural_conclusion.symmetrize_free_only: WRONG — inconsistent; spurious O(1) shift = scale·(h_Z h_N − τ^Z τ^N) reflecting the un-cancelled free factor.
structural_conclusion.log_ratio_cancellation: B_log shift = scale·log(S_free/S_atom); if S_atom=S_free (same nucleon content) the binding is UNCHANGED.
structural_conclusion.binding_signal: the residual log(S_free/S_atom) = the exact block-swapped bound symmetrization (task-1, S_Z×S_N), the small-Z refinement.
structural_conclusion.orbit_identity_does_NOT_trivialize_symme: atom_orbit_reduction.py proves tr_M(β_{Z,N})=tr_M(representative) with NO |orbit| factor — but that is RELABELING (σ leaves the word p…pn…n unchanged ⇒ conjugation β_σ W β_σ⁻¹, trace-preserving by Markov M1). The Young SYMMETRIZER is a DIFFERENT operation: it COMPOSES the block-swap braid, tr_M(W_atom·β_σ) (not conjugation), which the bonds make nontrivial. So S_atom = |G|⁻¹Σ_σ tr_M(W_atom·β_σ) is NOT trivially tr_M(W_atom); the orbit identity must not be used to shortcut it.
